title: Outsourced 24-Hour Vulnerability Reporting Desk (CRA)
one_liner: A retainer service that acts as the manufacturer's PSIRT: it watches for actively exploited vulnerabilities in their products' components and files the 24-hour early warning, follow-up notification and final report to the EU platform.
customer: Connected-device makers with 20-500 employees selling into the EU with no 24/7 security team: smart home, e-bikes and scooters, industrial sensors, routers, wearables, toys, EV chargers. Many are non-EU (US and Asian) firms.
problem: CRA reporting obligations began 11 Sep 2026: 24-hour reporting to ENISA for actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents, with fines up to EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover. Small makers have no on-call rota, no SBOM monitoring and no idea what 'actively exploited' means for their firmware. The briefing found almost no visible tooling aimed at them.
solution: A retainer that ingests each product's SBOM per firmware version, matches it continuously against exploited-vulnerability and threat feeds, triages 24/7 with a pre-agreed decision tree, and files the early warning, notification and final report with text approved by the client's named contact. It also runs coordinated disclosure and advisory publishing, plus quarterly tabletop drills. Software lets one analyst cover 30+ clients.
why_now: The reporting duty went live 17 days ago and the full regime follows in Dec 2027. Firms are discovering that the deadline is a staffing problem, not a document problem.
revenue_model: EUR 1,500-6,000/month retainer, incident surcharges, and EUR 5k annual tabletop exercises.
non_obvious_insight: A 24-hour clock makes this a staffing obligation, which small firms cannot meet alone but a pooled desk can, like outsourced DPO services. Each reported vulnerability also gives a natural upsell into SBOM and technical-file work.
first_30_days: Partner with two or three EU security consultancies or product-safety associations. Sell a EUR 2.5k one-day 'CRA reporting readiness audit' to 20 firms, convert 5-8 into EUR 2k/month retainers, and contract three part-time analysts across time zones.

title: Defensibility Desk for GenAI Document Review
one_liner: An independent validation service that samples, blind-reviews and documents the accuracy of AI-assisted document review so litigators can defend it to opposing counsel and judges.
customer: Litigation partners and e-discovery leads at mid-size firms (25-500 lawyers), corporate litigation departments, and ALSPs and e-discovery vendors moving first-pass review to LLMs.
problem: ALSPs are consolidating around AI-enabled workflows 'engineered around human review' (Repario acquired UnitedLex on 28 Sep 2026). Review has moved from TAR to LLM classification, and opposing parties and judges will ask for proof of recall and precision. Self-validation by the team that ran the review is neither independent nor consistent, and there is no accepted protocol for LLM review.
solution: A standard protocol: statistical sampling (elusion and recall estimates with confidence intervals), blind second-pass review by a bench of reviewers, adjudication of disagreements, drift checks across model versions, and a court-ready validation declaration with optional expert testimony. It plugs into Relativity, Everlaw and DISCO by API.
why_now: Generative-AI first-pass review went mainstream in 2025-26, private equity is rolling up ALSPs on the promise of AI plus human review, and judges are scrutinizing AI use in litigation.
revenue_model: $4-20k per matter validation, $60-250k/year programs for ALSPs, and hourly expert testimony.
non_obvious_insight: AI drives first-pass review cost toward zero, which makes independent validation the billable, defensible act, and independence is what gives it evidentiary weight (like an auditor). Displaced contract reviewers are a ready workforce for it.
first_30_days: Interview 15 e-discovery counsel and design the protocol with a statistician advisor. Run three pilot validations at $3-5k on closed matters and publish the protocol as a whitepaper to build credibility.

title: Same-Day Sub and Coach Bench for Home Daycares
one_liner: A membership that guarantees a licensed home daycare a vetted substitute within hours and, when a child's behavior threatens expulsion, an on-call early-childhood coach, so licensed slots stay open and parents keep their jobs.
customer: Licensed family child care providers (solo operators; start with about 300 in one metro or state). Co-payers: state agencies and child-care resource and referral (CCR&R) organizations with workforce-support funds, employers buying backup-care value, and Head Start partners.
problem: Childcare deserts are as much a retention problem as a construction problem. Family homes were the fastest-growing supply (+4.3% in 2024, versus +1.5% for centers), but one sick day closes a solo business, providers work 50-60 hour weeks, and average childcare worker pay is $33,140. Behavior challenges lead to expulsions, and few early-childhood mental health consultants exist to help. Each lost slot means a parent leaves work.
solution: 1) 'Slot Guarantee': a bench of background-checked, trained substitutes (retired teachers, early-education students, displaced parents) dispatched via app on a 2-hour target. 2) 'Calm Team': early-childhood coaches supervised by an infant-mental-health-endorsed clinician, deployed for observation and a behavior plan before expulsion. 3) Monthly Provider Circles of about 8 providers for peer support and reflective supervision. 4) Light back-office (attendance, billing).
why_now: Employer and family demand for childcare is rising with the 45F credit (40-50%) and the $7,500 dependent-care FSA, but supply is thin and fragile. Family homes are the growth segment, so protecting them is the cheapest new capacity. States are already funding workforce supports and early-childhood mental health consultation.
revenue_model: Provider membership of $79-129/mo including a few sub days per quarter, with extra sub hours billed at about $22/hr plus a fee. State or CCR&R contracts per provider. Behavior-coach visits at about $150 each or covered by state mental health consultation funds. Employer backup-care pools.
non_obvious_insight: Every desert plan builds new slots. The cheaper win is stopping existing slots from closing over sick days, burnout and expulsions. The real unit of childcare supply is a provider's mental state, and support for it is a bench of people, not an app.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 providers in one metro through Facebook groups and a CCR&R newsletter with a $59 founding-member rate. Assemble 15 substitutes from retired teachers and early-education students. Partner with one infant-mental-health clinician to lead the first Provider Circles. Approach the local CCR&R or county for a pilot fund, and track closures avoided as the headline metric.

title: Payee-Verification Network for the Live Music Business
one_liner: A shared, industry-vouched directory of who is really entitled to be paid in the touring economy (agencies, promoters, venues, production vendors), checked before every deposit wire.
customer: Independent and mid-size booking agencies, regional promoters, festivals, tour accountants and business managers, and production, trucking and staging vendors. Starting wedge is 50-200 person agencies and promoters that wire 50% artist deposits.
problem: Live touring runs on large advance wires: artist-guarantee deposits, production advances and vendor prepayments, with banking details passed through PDF contracts and email across dozens of small counterparties whose bookers, agents and accountants change often. That is ideal business-email-compromise territory (US BEC losses $3.05B in 2025 per FBI IC3), and now voice clones make 'the agent called to change the account' credible (a vendor report claims 680% year-over-year growth in voice-deepfake attacks). The FBI fund-freeze process recovered 58% of attempted funds but only when victims act fast, and each bank sees only its own side. Europe's mandatory Verification of Payee on euro transfers (from Oct 2025) checks name against IBAN only inside the euro zone, and the US has nothing similar, while tours mix currencies and countries.
solution: Verify each entity once (KYB, identity of authorised signers, bank account proven by micro-deposit or open banking) and publish signed payment instructions. Settlement spreadsheets and accounting tools check payees against the network before a wire is released, via a plug-in for spreadsheets, Slack and common accounting software. Any change of banking details triggers out-of-band, multi-party confirmation (agent, manager and accountant, never a reply-to email), with a 24-72 hour cooling-off for first payments. A bank hot-line handshake speeds recall and freeze on suspected misdirection. Each deal also generates a shared verbal code phrase to defeat cloned-voice calls.
why_now: IC3's 2025 numbers, AI-enabled scam operations earning about 4.5x more than others (Chainalysis, per briefing), and cheap voice cloning. Live Nation's $25.2B revenue and its arena buying show the sector's money is growing and consolidating, so more wires move through more small counterparties. EU Verification of Payee shows regulators' direction but leaves the cross-border and hybrid gap open.
revenue_model: SaaS of $99-499/month per verified entity. Per-payment verification fee of $2-5 or 0.02-0.05% for high-value wires. Bank and payments-provider licensing. Insurance partnerships where crime/cyber insurers discount premiums for network members.
non_obvious_insight: Payments-fraud vendors sell to banks and large corporates, but the live industry is thousands of small counterparties whose trust is relationship-based. The relationship graph (who is the legitimate agent, manager or accountant for whom) lives in people's heads, so the moat is a graph the industry vouches for itself. Once most deposits flow through the network, an unverified change-of-details request becomes an obvious red flag.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 mid-size booking agencies or tour accountants (the people whose wires get hit). Give them a free payment-instruction registry as a spreadsheet plus Slack or Chrome extension. Capture verified bank details for their top 100 counterparties. Run a consented voice-clone fire drill to create urgency. Charge $199/month per agency by day 60 and approach two insurers for premium-discount pilots.

title: Verified-Outreach Ledger for Government and Utilities
one_liner: A system where police, courts, tax offices and utilities log every outbound contact so residents can confirm in 20 seconds that they really called.
customer: County sheriffs and police departments, court clerks, county tax collectors, municipal utilities, and state benefits offices, buying through state cooperative contracts. Banks' fraud teams later.
problem: Law-enforcement impersonation drew about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B+ from Jan 2025 to Jul 2026, now with AI and fake video calls. The public message is 'the government never calls, hang up', which makes real outreach (jury duty, warrant notices, benefits recertification, shutoff notices) fail. Honest institutions can no longer reach people.
solution: Staff log each outreach in a lightweight tool or via CAD/CRM integration, and each contact gets a short code read aloud. Residents verify by calling or texting a verification number or visiting a page on the agency's .gov domain, which confirms agency, staffer, purpose and callback line. It also supports missed-contact reports and a library of 'we will never ask' scripts, and logs scam attempts for reporting.
why_now: The FBI's Sep 17 2026 PSA on law-enforcement impersonation makes the pain current, and video-call impersonation defeats 'just check the caller' advice. Google's on-device scam detection helps only one channel. Agencies have grant money for fraud outreach.
revenue_model: $3-12K per year per small agency via cooperative purchasing, $30-50K for a county-wide deployment, and per-message fees for banks and utilities.
non_obvious_insight: The second-order damage of the scam wave is trust deflation. Every warning that trains people to distrust callers makes legitimate callers less effective. The fix is to make the legitimate caller provable, not chase the fraudulent one.
first_30_days: Build a simple web tool plus a Twilio verification line in two weeks. Pilot with 3 sheriff's offices and one county court via a state sheriffs' association at $250 per month, and have them include codes on real warrant and jury notices.

title: PFAS Land-Application History Reports for Farmland
one_liner: A 'Phase I environmental site assessment' for PFAS on farmland, built from biosolids land-application records and upstream discharger data, sold to lenders, farmland funds and appraisers before the sensors exist.
customer: Farm Credit associations and ag banks, farmland investment funds, rural appraisers and title firms, and farmers or buyers who need to show a field is clean.
problem: EPA released Draft Guidance for Reducing Risk from PFOA and PFOS in Biosolids on July 1, 2026, noting that sewage sludge may carry PFAS from industrial dischargers, landfills and homes. Yet EPA's own FY2026 SBIR Phase I topics still ask small businesses to invent 'Treatment of PFAS in Wastewater Sewage Sludge and Biosolids' and 'Sensors to Detect PFAS in Environmental Matrices', so cheap field screening does not exist. Lenders and buyers are pricing farmland today with no way to know whether a field received sludge, from which plant, and with what upstream industrial inputs.
solution: A desktop screening report per parcel. It combines state biosolids land-application permits and site reports (obtained by scraping and automated public-records requests), the treatment plant's upstream industrial dischargers, soil and hydrology data, and a risk tier. Higher tiers trigger a sampling plan run by a partner lab using EPA Method 1633. Deliver in the lender's existing environmental-diligence workflow, and later offer an API.
why_now: The July 1, 2026 EPA draft guidance turns PFAS in biosolids from a research topic into something lenders must ask about. EPA's Sept 24, 2026 SBIR solicitation ($100k per Phase I, 6 months, closes Nov 8, 2026) is paying for the sensing tools, so cheap field tests are years away and records-based screening is the only option now.
revenue_model: $400 to $1,200 per desktop parcel report. $2k to $6k with coordinated sampling (margin on lab work). $20k to $60k per year API or portfolio subscriptions for lenders and farmland funds.
non_obvious_insight: The government is paying to invent PFAS sensors that don't exist yet, but the lend/buy/insure decision is being made now on paper records, so the winning product is the record-linkage layer, not the sensor. EPA's FY2026 SBIR Phase I topics list 1B (PFAS in sewage sludge and biosolids) and 2A (PFAS sensors in environmental matrices), $100,000 and 6 months each: https://www.epa.gov/sbir/how-apply-sbir-contract. EPA's biosolids page lists the July 1, 2026 Draft Guidance and states that sludge may carry PFAS from upstream dischargers: https://www.epa.gov/biosolids. Lenders already require site assessments for gas stations and dry cleaners, and a PFAS-on-farmland version is the missing sibling. Caveat: the EPA pages I could fetch gave no land-application tonnage or state-by-state record availability, so records access must be checked before committing to a state.
first_30_days: Pick 1 or 2 states where biosolids land-application permits are public (verify first). Assemble records for the 20 largest treatment plants and build 25 sample reports on real parcels. Approach 5 Farm Credit associations, 3 farmland funds and 5 rural appraisers with a free report on a parcel they already own or are underwriting. Sign a lab partner for sampling. Close the first 3 paid pilots at $400 to $1,200 per parcel.

title: Human Baseline Vault for AI Detection
one_liner: Proctored, ID-verified, unassisted human writing and speech, timestamped and sealed, sold first as ground truth for detector calibration and later as low-background evaluation data.
customer: AI-detection vendors, ed-tech firms and publishers, university integrity offices, trust-and-safety teams, and AI labs' evaluation teams.
problem: Studies report detector false-positive rates of 5-20% on native English and up to 61% on non-native writing. 25+ universities have restricted detectors, and a February 2026 New York court ordered Adelphi to expunge a student's AI accusation. Vendors cannot prove error rates by population because clean post-2022 human ground truth is unknowable, since everyone's 'human' data may be AI-assisted.
solution: Recruit 20k+ verified people across strata (non-native English, neurodivergent, technical, legal and academic writers, age bands) to write and speak in proctored sessions. Samples are timestamped and hash-anchored. Sell calibration sets and per-population false-positive certificates to detector vendors, then an annually refreshed vault as 'low-background steel' for evaluations and future disputes.
why_now: Over half of web traffic is automated and training and evaluation sets are increasingly contaminated. Lawsuits and university bans mean detector buyers now need error rates by population, and AI labs need uncontaminated human evaluation data.
revenue_model: $50-250k dataset licences, $20-75k per detector audit and certificate, and annual refresh subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Like pre-1945 steel free of nuclear fallout, verified pre-contamination human data gets more valuable every year, and its value lies in the chain of custody, not the text itself.
first_30_days: Recruit 500 participants through two university partners for a native versus non-native pilot. Pitch two detector vendors and one ed-tech firm. Publish an independent study on false positives by population to earn press.

title: Pre-Cut Electrical Kits Per House Plan
one_liner: A regional kitting shop ships each production home's wiring as pre-cut, labeled, bundled kits so a helper pulls and a journeyman only terminates and inspects.
customer: Electrical subcontractors serving production and spec builders (5-100 homes a year), and builders in data-center-hot markets such as Texas.
problem: Data centers absorb electricians (nearly a third of the shortage; journeymen on overtime gross $130-170K, vendor stat), and Texas builders report electrical delays of up to 2 months. Meanwhile much rough-in time goes to measuring, cutting and pulling, which does not need a licensed person's minutes.
solution: For each repeat plan, generate a wire schedule and build kits: cable pre-cut and labeled by room and circuit, boxes pre-assembled, home runs pre-bundled, panel schedule pre-printed, delivered in numbered bins by phase. Lower-skill pullers or apprentices do most of the rough-in under supervision, and the journeyman terminates and inspects.
why_now: Electrician arbitrage from data-center overtime, builders with idle houses waiting on electrical, and digital plan libraries that expose structured circuit data. Wire-processing machines are cheap and used equipment is plentiful.
revenue_model: Materials plus 15-25%, or $2-4K per home, with a share of labor savings. Licensing the process to kitting shops in other metros.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is journeyman minutes on tasks a journeyman does not need to do. Commercial contractors have prefabbed for decades, but residential never did because labor was cheap, and now the ROI is large.
first_30_days: Pick one production builder's most repeated plan. Hire an ex-electrician estimator and buy or rent a used cut-and-label machine. Sell kits for five homes to the builder's electrical sub and measure hours saved per house.

title: Population-Diverse iPSC Villages for Drug Safety
one_liner: Pool 50-100 genetically diverse donor iPSC lines in one dish and read out each donor's drug response by genotype, giving pharma a 'clinical trial in a dish' for roughly the cost of one experiment.
customer: Pharma safety-pharmacology and toxicology groups, oligonucleotide and gene-editing developers worried about idiosyncratic toxicity, and NAM-adopting CROs.
problem: The NAM debate centers on organ complexity, but single-donor organoids cannot show the population variability behind idiosyncratic liver injury or QT prolongation. FDA now wants 'adequately validated' methods, and conventional multi-donor testing costs n times as much.
solution: A curated, consented and commercially licensable diverse iPSC panel differentiated to cardiomyocytes or neurons (where villages are best proven), dosed with compound series and demultiplexed by genotype through scRNA-seq. Deliver donor-level dose-response distributions, genotype-linked sensitivity and concordance versus clinical outcomes.
why_now: Village-in-a-dish methods have matured, with CIRM-funded pooled iPSC-cardiomyocyte 'clinical trial in a dish' work and a 2026 methods perspective in Frontiers in Bioengineering. Greenstone Biosciences is an early commercial competitor in cardiac models. The FDA rule gives sponsors a reason to buy, and scRNA-seq costs keep falling.
revenue_model: $60-150k per compound panel, $300k/year subscriptions, and licensing the panel to CROs.
non_obvious_insight: Pooling collapses the cost of diversity: n=100 costs roughly what n=5 does. The moat is the consented, well-characterized line panel and a genotype-linked outcomes database, not the assay, which anyone can copy.
first_30_days: License 30-50 lines from public repositories, checking commercial-use consent. Build a cardiomyocyte village. Test 20 reference cardiotoxic and safe drugs and publish the concordance. Pitch 10 safety-pharmacology leads on $30k pilots.

title: Protein Cartridges for Heavy Rare-Earth Polishing
one_liner: Skid-mounted cartridges of engineered lanmodulin-type proteins that separate heavy rare earths (Dy, Tb) from magnet-recycling leachate without long solvent-extraction chains.
customer: Magnet recyclers and small separators whose processes end in mixed rare-earth concentrates, plus DoD- and DOE-backed pilot programs.
problem: Recovery projects often end with mixed concentrates that still need separation, which conventionally takes hundreds of solvent-extraction stages that China dominates. Heavy rare earths are the acute chokepoint after China's 2025 export controls.
solution: Protein-based sorbents (naturally lanthanide-binding proteins, studied at Penn State and Lawrence Livermore) engineered for heavy-RE selectivity. They are packed in modular columns as a polishing step at ambient conditions. The business model is cartridge consumables plus skid rental.
why_now: Heavy rare earths are now a stated national-security bottleneck, DOE announced $134M for demonstrations in June 2026, and AI protein design has made engineering selectivity a computation problem instead of a decade-long screen.
revenue_model: Consumable cartridge sales plus skid lease. Early revenue from SBIR grants and paid pilots.
non_obvious_insight: Rare-earth chemistry fights in a sea of near-identical ions, while proteins evolved to tell lanthanides apart. The hard part is now designing the scaffold, not discovering the effect.
first_30_days: License or partner with a university lab. Run bench tests on real recycler leachate. Apply to DOE and DoD SBIR programs. Sign 2 recyclers to paid pilots.

title: One Annual Fee for Every Mandatory EU Representative
one_liner: A roll-up of small EU authorised-representative shops that bundles every legally required local presence (GDPR Art. 27, AI Act, Data Act, product safety, CRA) into one liability-bearing annual contract for non-EU companies.
customer: US, UK, Israeli, Indian and Asian SaaS, AI and hardware companies ($2M-$200M revenue) selling in the EU without an EU entity. Bought by founders, GCs and ops leads.
problem: Several EU regimes require non-EU companies to name someone in the EU who can be held to account: GDPR Art. 27, AI Act authorised representatives for high-risk and GPAI providers, Data Act legal representative, product-safety responsible person, an optional CRA authorised representative (background knowledge; verify each). Today each comes from a different vendor, many are one-person shops or law firms wary of liability, and none coordinate.
solution: Acquire three to six small rep businesses (typically hundreds to a couple thousand clients on sticky annual fees), keep their brands, and rebuild operations with automation for inbound regulator and data-subject mail triage, translation and escalation. Add an EU law-firm panel as backstop and sell one bundle with a shared register of representations, one invoice and standard playbooks, priced for the liability.
why_now: GPAI duties applied Aug 2025 with enforcement from Aug 2026, Data Act obligations arrived Sep 2025 and Sep 2026, and CRA reporting started 11 Sep 2026, so many non-EU firms suddenly face three or four rep obligations at once. AI lowers the cost of delivering the service.
revenue_model: EUR 3-15k/year per client bundle, 70-80% renewal, acquisitions at roughly 1-2x revenue, and upsell to compliance retainers.
non_obvious_insight: When AI makes drafting free, the scarce good is someone in the EU who can be sued. Liability-bearing presence has pricing power and stickiness, and becoming the address regulators write to is a distribution moat.
first_30_days: List 30 small EU rep providers and approach five owners about a white-label or revenue-share deal that leads to acquisition. Sell the bundle to 10 US SaaS and AI firms through founder communities at EUR 4k and obtain a professional-indemnity quote.

title: Turn Half-Empty School Wings Into Child Care
one_liner: A turnkey operator that leases empty classrooms in half-empty Title I elementary schools and runs licensed infant, toddler and before/after-school care in them.
customer: School districts that lease the space (landlord side). Revenue comes from parents (including those on state child-care subsidies), state pre-K funds, and employers or the district itself buying slots for staff.
problem: Birth-rate decline has left many elementary schools 20 to 40 percent empty, and districts are closing buildings. Yet the neighborhood has no infant care, teachers quit over child care, and before/after-school waitlists run for months. Empty rooms cost the district no visible money, so nobody champions them, and district counsel treats a sublease as a liability risk.
solution: Sell a feasibility and licensing audit ($5k to $15k) covering egress, restrooms, square footage per child, fencing, a separate entrance, and the fire marshal. Then operate the program as a license-holding subtenant. Staff it with cross-trained paras and neighborhood parents. Accept subsidy vouchers and state pre-K slots. Give priority to school staff and Title I families, and keep before- and after-school care in the same building. The district gets rent plus a utilities share, and the operator keeps a thin margin.
why_now: Enrollment declines and school-closure fights are peaking. The 2025 tax law raised the employer child-care tax credit starting in 2026, which helps districts and employers underwrite staff slots. Several states are expanding subsidized or universal child care. Federal after-school funding uncertainty in 2025 also opened a gap for paid programs.
revenue_model: Tuition and subsidy revenue for the operator. One-time feasibility and licensing fees. Optional management fee if a nonprofit or district holds the license.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone talks about reusing closed schools. The money is in schools that stay open but are half-empty, where a wing can be subleased tomorrow with no rezoning. Elementary buildings already meet many child-care code items: kid-height restrooms, exits, a playground and a kitchen. The principal knows this from living in the building. The blocker is the district's lease template and its fear of liability, and both are solvable with paperwork.
first_30_days: Map licensing rules in one state and find a nonprofit child-care operator willing to hold the license. Pitch 5 superintendents and principals with a two-page space-utilization audit and a sample lease. Sell three $5k feasibility audits to fund the pilot, and use waitlists from existing before/after-school programs as proof of demand.

title: Bonded Escorts for Sedated Outpatient Patients
one_liner: A background-checked adult who legally receives your discharge instructions and takes you home after a colonoscopy or other sedated procedure, sold to the clinics that lose the slot when you have no ride.
customer: Independent GI groups and ambulatory surgery centers pay $65-95 per escorted visit. Solo agers and estranged or far-from-family adults pay $99-149 directly as a fallback.
problem: Most sedation centers will not proceed unless a responsible adult picks the patient up and hears the discharge instructions, and many refuse to release a sedated patient to a rideshare driver. Patients with no spouse, no nearby family, or no friend willing to sit through the aftermath of a bowel prep cancel, delay screening, or no-show. The clinic eats an empty high-margin slot. The patient feels embarrassed to ask and avoids the procedure.
solution: A regional network of vetted, insured escorts drawn from CNAs, retired nurses, EMTs and nursing students. The clinic scheduler adds one line to the booking call: 'No escort? Tap here and we will send one.' The escort meets the patient at the door, is named on the chart as the responsible adult, receives instructions, rides home with the patient, stays 20-30 minutes until the patient is settled, and texts a family contact. A clinic dashboard shows escort confirmed, so day-of cancellations for this reason disappear. Later add the required 24-hour post-anesthesia overnight companion, then cataract, oral surgery, and cosmetic and orthopedic day surgery.
why_now: The USPSTF lowered the colorectal screening start age to 45, which added millions of eligible patients. Procedures keep migrating to ambulatory surgery centers, which run on tight slot economics. The share of older adults living alone (solo agers) is at a record high. Checkr-style vetting and Stripe Connect-style payouts let a tiny team stand up a bonded, insured gig network in weeks. No incumbent sells 'the adult on the chart' to schedulers.
revenue_model: Per-visit fee paid by the clinic ($65-95, escort keeps about 60%) or patient-pay ($99-149). Add-ons include overnight post-anesthesia sitters billed hourly. Later, Medicare Advantage plans buy escort-with-transport as a supplemental benefit.
non_obvious_insight: The escort rule is a liability policy, not a medical one, so what the clinic needs is a credentialed name on the chart that satisfies the discharge nurse, not a ride. Nobody sells to the scheduling desk, where the cancellation leak is measured in dollars per slot. The patient's real barrier is shame at asking a friend to witness a colonoscopy, which a professional stranger removes.
first_30_days: Pick one metro. Recruit 15 escorts from nursing-school boards and retired-nurse groups. Get a general and professional liability quote and run Checkr checks. Visit 10 GI practices and offer a free 30-day pilot where they pay only when an escort saves a slot that would have cancelled. Launch a landing page and a Twilio text line, and buy Google Ads on searches like 'colonoscopy no one to drive me home'. Run dispatch from a spreadsheet. Goal: 40 escorted procedures and 3 signed clinics.

title: Coder-Signed Reasonable-Value Reports for Injury Defense
one_liner: A 48-hour, coder-certified benchmark report that tells defense lawyers and auto carriers what a letter-of-protection medical bill is actually worth.
customer: Insurance defense law firms and auto-carrier litigation/SIU units handling bodily-injury claims in tort-reform states (Florida, Georgia, Texas, Louisiana first). Volume firms pay per report. Carriers pay monthly.
problem: Plaintiff-side injury cases increasingly rest on treatment provided under letters of protection (LOP), where the provider is paid from the settlement and bills at a private rate card. Defense lawyers have to show what the care is really worth. Today that means a $3-5k billing expert, a slow turnaround, and a fight over methodology. Most claims examiners cannot read a CMS-1500 or UB-04, so inflated bills mostly get paid or settled at face value.
solution: Intake the itemized bill and records. Map every line to CPT/HCPCS and revenue codes and flag unbundling (e.g. 99215-25 plus separate injection administration, physician-owned ASC facility fees stacked on the professional fee, stacked imaging reads). Benchmark each line against Medicare multiples, hospital-posted commercial negotiated rates from price-transparency files, and local percentiles. The output is a Daubert-hardened PDF signed by a certified coder (CPC/CCS) with an optional expert declaration or testimony upsell. It is a methodology plus a template, so the marginal cost per report is about an hour of coder time.
why_now: Florida's 2023 tort reform made LOP arrangements discoverable and admitted evidence of amounts actually paid. Georgia's 2025 tort reform pushed similar rules, and other states are copying. Hospital price-transparency rules that took full effect in 2026 now require actual payment amounts where rates are percentages or algorithms, so a defensible local benchmark exists for the first time.
revenue_model: $295-$695 per report. Expert declaration or testimony at $1,500-$3,500. $2-5k/month subscriptions for carriers and volume firms with a report quota. Gross margin is high because coders are paid per report as contractors.
non_obvious_insight: Inside a hospital, chargemaster prices are understood to be fiction, and every biller knows what things really get paid. Injury lawyers have been arguing about 'reasonable value' without that insider map. Certified coders also know the tells of bills built for litigation rather than payment: modifier-25 patterns, unbundled facility fees, and E/M levels that no insurer would ever pay. The market is starved of people credentialed and willing to say so on paper. The moat is a coder bench plus a methodology that survives cross-examination, not software.
first_30_days: Recruit 3-5 CPC/CCS coders (ex-hospital, remote, contractors) and one defense-attorney advisor to review the methodology memo. Build the report template from the free Medicare fee schedules plus a few metro-area price-transparency files. Cold-email about 100 Florida and Georgia defense firms and claims managers, and offer 5 free reports on live cases in exchange for a methodology review and a testimonial. Convert the first 3-5 to $349 per report, then price the expert declaration as an add-on.

title: Peak-Window Uptime Plans for Fishing Boats
one_liner: A seasonal membership that pre-stages each boat's likely failure parts and rebuilt swap components in the harbor, provides RSW and hydraulic mechanics on call, and later adds a paid lost-peak-days cover.
customer: Bristol Bay and Prince William Sound drift and set net owners, plus seiners, who pay $2,000-4,000 per boat per season. A fleet of a few hundred boats is a $1M-plus business. Later an insurance partner underwrites the lost-time cover.
problem: Most of a boat's year is earned in about 10-14 days. With 2026's $1.72/lb, a busy boat can earn $5-15K a day at peak. Hull and machinery insurance pays for repair, never for the lost fishing days. A raw-water impeller, hydraulic hose, reel motor, fuel filter or failed RSW system takes a boat out for three days because the part is on a barge or a bush flight that's booked solid. The whole fleet breaks the same dozen components in the same ten days.
solution: Catalog the top 15-20 failure modes by engine and hydraulic setup. Stage member-funded kits in secure containers at Naknek, Dillingham, Egegik and similar harbors by June 1. Hold a rotating pool of rebuilt swap cores (injection pumps, hydraulic pumps, reel motors). Contract freelance diesel, hydraulic and RSW mechanics on retainer for guaranteed response times. Members can order from the grounds by satellite text. Phase two: verified downtime (AIS, dock check-in, mechanic log) triggers a fixed per-day payment during declared peak windows through an MGA partner.
why_now: The 2026 price rebound made every fishing day worth much more than in 2025. The fleet is aging. RSW is now paid for (about $0.15/lb bonus at some processors), yet the regional development association is funding apprentices because there aren't enough RSW technicians. Starlink lets skippers order parts and report faults from the fishing grounds.
revenue_model: Membership fees of $2-4K per boat per season, parts and swap-core margin, mechanic call-out fees, and a later per-day parametric lost-time premium shared with the underwriter.
non_obvious_insight: Downtime costs are about timing, not repair. The scarce resource at peak is the right part on the right beach within hours, and nobody sells that. It works as pooled inventory: because the fleet fails predictably, a small stockpile insures hundreds of boats. Insurance pooling for parts is cheaper and faster to launch than insurance pooling for money.
first_30_days: Interview 30 skippers and mechanics at the November Pacific Marine Expo in Seattle and by phone with Naknek and Dillingham crews. Build the failure-mode parts list by engine and hydraulic setup. Pre-sell 40 memberships with $500 deposits by February. Line up two freelance mechanics and one RSW tech. Rent a container in one harbor and stage the first 40 boats' kits by June 1.

title: Vet-Verified Escrow for Puppy Purchases
one_liner: Buyer funds sit in escrow and release to the seller only after a licensed vet exam confirms the animal is healthy and the microchip matches.
customer: First-time online puppy and kitten buyers (mostly Gen Z and millennials), plus ethical breeders, rescues and rehoming sellers who lose sales to scammers. Partner clinics are the fulfillment side and insurers are the third payer.
problem: Pet-purchase scams are a top online-fraud category inside the FTC's record $15.9B of 2025 scam losses. Deposits go by Zelle, Cash App or gift card and are irreversible. Legitimate breeders cannot prove trustworthiness. Sick puppies (parvo and congenital problems) show up days after a sale, and a vet shortage means new-patient slots are scarce, so buyers skip the check.
solution: The buyer pays via card or ACH into escrow. Release requires a 72-hour exam at a partner clinic confirming health, microchip and vaccination records; failure means refund minus fee. Part of the escrow fee pays the clinic for the exam, so the clinic gains a new client with prepaid revenue. The exam visit also enrolls the pet in insurance while it is clean of pre-existing conditions, for an acquisition fee. Extensions: lost-pet reward escrow released on a microchip scan, and stud and rehoming fees.
why_now: Record scam losses and irreversible peer-to-peer payments make buyers and platforms desperate for protection. Only 48.2% of practices proactively recommend insurance, so insurers need better first-year distribution. Clinics are capacity-constrained and want reliable new patients. Delayed-payout marketplace payment APIs make escrow cheap to build.
revenue_model: 4-5% escrow fee, $40-60 insurer acquisition fee per enrolled pet, and clinic exam fees funded from the escrow. Sellers can pay for a verified-breeder badge.
non_obvious_insight: The vet exam is the only trusted, licensed, in-person oracle in the pet-purchase chain, so use it as the escrow release condition. Because the fee funds the visit, the clinic gets a paid new client, which turns the vet shortage into a pull instead of a friction.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 ethical breeders or rescues and 5 clinics in one metro. Build on Stripe Connect delayed payouts. Market to breed groups on Facebook and puppy-advice communities, and offer the first 50 transactions at a discount for testimonials.

title: AI-Aware E&O Cover for Solo Consultants
one_liner: A specialty insurance agency for laid-off professionals turned solo consultants whose errors-and-omissions cover may quietly exclude AI-assisted work, with premiums discounted for logged verification workflows.
customer: Solo and 2-10-person consultancies (fractional CFOs, marketing and analytics freelancers, dev contractors, HR and ops consultants) pay $400-1,500 a year in premium. The agency earns roughly 15-20% commission.
problem: Large carriers have reportedly sought AI-liability exclusions, so a freelancer who used AI on a deliverable can find a claim denied. Client contracts increasingly demand E&O plus AI-use reps. Newly independent laid-off professionals never read the policy language.
solution: A retail agency that places policies with carriers offering affirmative AI coverage (an MGA program later). A lightweight verification log (source checks, review sign-off) yields an underwriting-friendly attestation that lowers price. A contract clause checker flags indemnities, plus a template AI-use disclosure for clients.
why_now: Carrier AI-exclusion filings surfaced in late 2025, layoffs are creating a wave of new independents, and enterprise procurement now asks vendors for AI-use attestations. AI-liability startups target enterprises, not solos.
revenue_model: Commissions of 15-20%, MGA fees later, and a $10-a-month verification-log tool.
non_obvious_insight: The gap is one of underwriting information: how AI-assisted work is actually verified versus what the policy assumes. A logged verification workflow is data an insurer will pay for with lower prices. Premiums are too small for big brokers to chase, so a new insured class goes unserved.
first_30_days: Partner with a licensed E&O producer (or get licensed). Read the AI language of 10 carriers and publish a 'Does your E&O cover AI?' checker and newsletter for laid-off and freelancer communities. Bind the first 20 policies.

title: Scam Recovery Desk for Community Banks
one_liner: Banks buy scam detection, but the untapped money is recovery: stablecoin issuers, receiving banks and exchanges can freeze funds if someone asks fast and correctly.
customer: Community banks and credit unions ($500M-$10B assets) that increasingly eat scam reimbursements. American Banker (2026-07-22) puts bank-side scam losses at $68B, against the FTC's $15.9B of consumer-reported losses.
problem: A community bank's fraud analyst has hours before funds move on. They don't know who to call at receiving banks, exchanges or issuer compliance desks. They have no standard evidence pack, so recoveries run to a few percent and losses are written off as a cost of doing business.
solution: A 24/7 recovery desk plus software. When a victim reports a scam, the desk traces the funds (wire, Zelle and ACH recall, plus on-chain tracing for crypto off-ramps). It sends recall, 314(b) and law-enforcement freeze requests with pre-validated evidence packs to a maintained directory of receiving-institution and issuer contacts, then tracks outcomes. The desk is paid a share of every dollar recovered.
why_now: FTC losses hit a record $15.9B in 2025, and scam flows increasingly touch stablecoins. The Senate Democrats' Tether report (2026-09-28) raises pressure on issuers to respond quickly, and GENIUS-era issuers must be able to honor lawful freeze orders (verify exact text).
revenue_model: 15-25% contingency on recovered funds plus a flat monthly retainer for 24/7 coverage.
non_obvious_insight: Recovery rates depend on speed and relationships, not analytics, so a maintained contact directory and playbook is an operations moat. Stablecoins are counterintuitively the most freezable scam rail, more so than wires or Zelle, if you know the freeze path.
first_30_days: Offer five community banks a free post-mortem of their last 90 days of scam cases and estimate the recoverable share. Hire two ex-bank fraud investigators. Sign two contingency pilots and build the first version of the issuer and receiving-bank contact directory.

title: Lights-Out Receiving Network for Driverless Freight
one_liner: On-demand night-shift dock crews plus remotely operable gates and dock doors so driverless trucks arriving at 3 a.m. actually get inspected and unloaded.
customer: Driverless-truck operators and their shipper and receiver customers, distribution centers with thin overnight staffing, and brokers offering autonomous lanes.
problem: Driverless trucks run around the clock, but most receivers have no dock labor, yard checks or inspectors at night. The CVSA enhanced-inspection clearance lasts 24 hours and requires a trained inspector, and hub-to-hub handoffs leave 'hundreds of dollars' of human cost per transfer. The PrePass/Kodiak bypass integration is live only in Texas and Louisiana.
solution: Three pieces. First, a network of trained ex-driver and yard-tech turnaround crews for walk-arounds, sensor cleaning and trailer checks. Second, a $3-6k remote gate and dock-door kit so the AV can check in and get a door. Third, on-call unload crews, with everything dispatched from one app and priced per turn below the cost of a human transfer.
why_now: Aurora is exiting 2026 with about 200 driverless trucks and targets 30,000 by 2030, California's driverless-truck rules took effect on April 28, 2026, and the Teamsters sued on August 5. Hiring retrained drivers into new roles also buys political goodwill.
revenue_model: $150-400 per truck turn, equipment lease or subscription for gate and dock kits, and a per-lane subscription for receivers.
non_obvious_insight: Autonomy shifts the constraint from driver hours to dock hours: the truck no longer sleeps, but the receiver does. The rent moves to whoever owns the human touch at the endpoints, and hiring displaced drivers turns opposition into a labor supply.
first_30_days: Pick one corridor where driverless trucks already run (for example Fort Worth to El Paso). Sign LOIs with 2 shippers on that lane for overnight receiving, recruit 10 ex-drivers or yard techs, build a simple dispatch app and target first paid turns within 90 days.

title: Government Property Control Kit for New Defense Makers
one_liner: A fixed-price property-system-in-a-box (tags, procedures, mock audit, reconciliation) that keeps first-time defense manufacturers from failing their government property audit and having payments withheld.
customer: New-entrant defense manufacturers (drone, munitions second-source and component startups) and small machine shops that receive government-furnished property, plus primes that flow the property clauses down and want their subs certified.
problem: Contractors holding government-furnished property must run a property management system with receiving reports, physical inventory, loss and damage reporting, and reconciliation to the contract's property list. If the government disapproves the system, contracting officers can direct payment withholds. Small shops run this on spreadsheets and no one is the accountable hand-receipt holder. Property administrators cannot coach, and consultants bill $200-400 an hour.
solution: A packaged offering. A one-day on-site 'mock property system analysis' run by former property administrators. Asset tagging and mobile scanning. Templated procedures, forms and a monthly reconciliation to the contract property list. Audit-ready binder and annual physical inventory support. Ongoing loss/damage/destruction reporting and excess-property disposition paperwork. Position it to program managers, not compliance officers, as schedule protection.
why_now: The Revolutionary FAR Overhaul rewrote Part 45 (Government Property), with model deviation text implemented from November 2025, so many contractors are rereading their obligations. Defense spending and drone and munitions ramp-ups are pulling venture-backed hardware companies and first-time subs into contracts with government-furnished property. CMMC phase-ins compete for the same small compliance budgets, so property control gets ignored until an audit finds it.
revenue_model: Mock audit at $6-15k, then $500-2,000 a month for software plus fractional property-officer support, plus per-asset tagging fees. Prime-sponsored programs where a prime pays to certify its sub base.
non_obvious_insight: The property system is about 90% behavior and 10% software: who signs for what, and whether there is an unbroken trail from receipt to disposition. Auditors find the same handful of deficiencies again and again (no receiving report, no physical inventory, no reconciliation, no loss report), so a checklist-driven fixed-price service works better than custom consulting. The strongest sponsor is the prime, because a sub's disapproved system threatens the prime's own schedule and cash.
first_30_days: Pull first-time awardees from SBIR/STTR winners and public contract awards that carry government-furnished property. Offer 10 of them a $2,500 one-day GFP health check. Publish a one-page 'seven findings auditors keep writing' as lead magnet. Partner with a regional APEX Accelerator for referrals and a CMMC registered provider organization for cross-sell. Turn the first 3 engagements into a templated binder and a simple scanning workflow before building any software.

title: Risk and Insurance Stack for Pickleball Venues
one_liner: Incident logging, e-waivers, court-safety audits and an insurance program that make independent racquet venues insurable at fair prices.
customer: Independent indoor and outdoor pickleball and padel venue operators, plus HOAs and municipal recreation departments.
problem: Indoor pickleball operators report difficulty finding coverage, typical policies carry $1-5M general liability, injuries rose about 6.8x between 2017 and 2022, and noise disputes now end in lawsuits. Insurers lack venue-level data, so they price the category rather than the operator.
solution: Step one: $149-299 per month software with e-waivers, incident reporting, a photo-evidence court, lighting and fencing audit checklist and staff training. Step two: use the aggregated data to place operators with specialty carriers as a broker or MGA and negotiate premium credits for documented venues.
why_now: Venue counts have boomed while commentators now say the boom is starting to crack, which makes insurers and lenders demand evidence; no standard exists.
revenue_model: SaaS $149-299 per venue per month plus 10-15 percent broker or MGA commission on premiums of $8-30k per policy.
non_obvious_insight: Data is the product: when insurers lack venue-level evidence they price to the average, so the operator who documents beats the average. Start as software, then capture the insurance economics.
first_30_days: Partner with a licensed broker, audit 10 venues in one metro, produce an insurer-ready risk dossier for each, and take 20 dossiers to two specialty carriers.

title: Voice-Clone-Proof Verbal Deals for Grain and Cattle
one_liner: A two-channel confirmation step and verified-payee ledger that makes phone-and-handshake commodity deals safe from cloned voices and redirected payments.
customer: Regional grain elevators and co-ops, livestock auction markets and order buyers, ag input retailers, and the ag lenders that finance them.
problem: Agriculture runs on calls: bids, forward contracts, cattle sales, input prepays and cash rents, with confirmation by email. About 3 seconds of audio can clone a farmer's or merchandiser's voice, and BEC cost $3.05B in 2025. Retail beef hit a record $9.64/lb, contract sizes are up, and farm distress attracts fake-buyer scams. Small operations have no fraud team, and cross-bank recovery through the FBI's process is rarely accessible to them.
solution: Verify each farmer's bank account ownership once, with a passphrase or app approval. Any verbal contract above a threshold, or any change of payee, triggers an out-of-band push approval or a callback to a pre-registered number. Settlement pays only to verified accounts. Integrate with grain accounting and auction-clerk systems. Extend to cash-rent payments to older landlords and to the December input prepay season.
why_now: Voice cloning is mainstream. Chainalysis reports impersonation scams up 1,400% with average payments up 253%, and the FBI's Sept 17 2026 PSA cites AI video calls in law-enforcement impersonation. The December prepay season is about ten weeks away, and record livestock prices raise the stakes.
revenue_model: $300-800 a month per elevator or auction location plus $0.50-2 per verified payment. Lenders pay per portfolio, and cyber insurers may give premium credits.
non_obvious_insight: In agriculture the voice is the credential. Forty-year relationships mean nobody asks for ID, and voice cloning breaks the oldest trust protocol in commodity trading. The paying customer is the elevator or auction, which bears misdirected settlements, not the farmer. The tool plugs into settlement systems that banks cannot see.
first_30_days: Interview 20 elevator merchandisers and controllers. Pilot with 2 regional co-ops during harvest settlements using a bank account-owner check plus text push approval. Present to auction-market clerk groups. Ask a cyber-insurance broker about premium credits. Offer a December prepay fraud drill.

title: Dead Capital: Succession Kits for Diaspora Families
one_liner: A flat-fee, advocate-supervised 'estate file' service that gets a dead parent's or grandfather's land, shares and dormant accounts legally transferred, sold to the adult children who pay from Nairobi, Dallas or Dubai.
customer: Salaried urban and diaspora Kenyans aged 30-55 whose rural parents or grandparents died (or are old) with land still registered in a dead person's name. They pay from abroad or from the city. A secondary B2B payer is any SACCO, coop or bank that needs cleared successions before it releases deposits or lends against land.
problem: Most rural family land is still titled to a dead grandfather or father because nobody completed succession. The process needs a chief's letter, a death certificate, consents from every heir, gazettement, a wait before confirmation of grant, and then transmission at the land registry, which is often 1-3 years and many trips. Until it is done the land cannot be leased, mortgaged, subdivided or cleanly sold, siblings fight, and the deceased's SACCO deposits, coop shares, insurance and pension sit unclaimed. The real blocker is coordinating 8 to 20 relatives to sign, not the court.
solution: Wedge product is a 'Family Estate Map' for roughly KES 15-25k (pricing to be tested). The child sends photos of the title, IDs, death certificate and old share certificates over WhatsApp. An LLM pipeline extracts names and parcel numbers, handles the multiple-name and spelling-variant problem in Kenyan naming, builds the family tree and likely heirs, and lists the consents needed. It runs official land searches and asset-discovery letters to SACCOs, coops, insurers and the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority, then outputs a court-ready bundle of forms and affidavits. A home-county field agent collects the chief's letter and relatives' signatures or thumbprints, with video proof of consent. Partner advocates then file and shepherd the case at their own scale fees. Later upsells are surveyor subdivision and lease or loan readiness.
why_now: The generation that took up land in the 1960s-80s through settlement schemes and land-buying companies is dying now, so the succession backlog is peaking. Diaspora remittances are near record levels (roughly US$5bn a year), and families increasingly ask 'sort out the land' rather than 'build a house'. Digitised land records (Ardhisasa) and court e-filing reduce physical running, though their current coverage needs checking. LLMs can now read messy scanned title and ID documents and draft forms in English while chatting with clients in Swahili. I could not run live searches, so verify current UFAA agent rules, court e-filing scope for successions, and fee schedules before building.
revenue_model: Flat fee per estate file, paid by M-Pesa or card from abroad. Advocate fees are billed by the advocates themselves, so the company sells software and case management and does not split fees with non-lawyers. Asset discovery is a flat add-on fee, not a percentage cut of UFAA payouts, because UFAA discourages middlemen taking a share. B2B revenue is per cleaned member estate from SACCOs and coops. Later there is referral income from surveyors and land-backed lenders once titles are clean.
non_obvious_insight: Rural Kenya's biggest pool of unused collateral is land trapped in the name of the dead. The bottleneck is family coordination and evidence gathering, so the product is a coordination workflow sold to the sibling who has money and guilt, not a land registry or a lawyer marketplace. VCs looking at land-tech miss that the payer is the diaspora child, not the farmer.
first_30_days: Pick one county (for example Murang'a or Kakamega) and recruit two advocates who already do succession work. Build intake on WhatsApp Business, Airtable and an LLM extraction script. Sell 10 files at a pilot discount through your own family network, church and alumni groups, and diaspora WhatsApp and Facebook groups such as Kenyans in Texas or the UK. Publish a free 'Is your family land still in a dead man's name?' checker as lead-gen. Track days from intake to gazettement as the core metric.

title: Frozen Models: Long-Term Support for AI Deployments
one_liner: A 'Red Hat for AI models': host specific model versions with a written 5-7 year availability guarantee, reproducibility pack and migration diff-testing, for companies that cannot let their AI change under them.
customer: Model-risk, compliance and QA leads at mid-size banks, insurers, health-tech and pharma-adjacent firms, and legal-tech teams that have validated an AI workflow. Later, AI-companion products and their users, who care about persona continuity.
problem: Frontier labs retire models on 12-18 month cycles. Every retirement forces re-running evals, re-validating prompts and re-documenting for auditors. When OpenAI retired GPT-4o from ChatGPT on Feb 13, 2026, it set off the #Keep4o backlash, proving people and firms treat model behavior as something they depend on.
solution: Pin and host frozen snapshots of open-weight models (and customers' own fine-tunes), with contractual availability through a stated year, a fixed and documented inference stack (versions, quantization, seeds), and a change-control pack (model card, eval suite, audit logs). Add a migration service that replays your real traffic through old and new models and produces a behavior-diff report when you choose to upgrade.
why_now: Deprecation cycles have shortened and the 2026 GPT-4o episode made instability visible outside engineering teams. Regulators and auditors increasingly ask for documented change control on AI systems, and open-weight models are now good enough for many bounded enterprise tasks. Nobody is selling stability itself as the product.
revenue_model: Monthly hosting subscription plus per-token usage, one-time change-control pack fees, and per-migration diff-testing engagements.
non_obvious_insight: Enterprises don't buy the best model, they buy the model that won't change. Each frontier release is a validation event for regulated buyers, so a vendor whose product is boring stability (like Ubuntu LTS or RHEL) has a natural niche, and the cost side is cheap because old open weights run on modest GPUs. The consumer angle (keeping a beloved persona alive) adds emotional stickiness that pure infra players can't match.
first_30_days: Interview 20 model-risk and compliance leads in banks and insurers. Publish a one-page 'frozen model SLA' with pricing. Host three open-weight snapshots on rented GPUs with a documented inference stack. Close two design partners at $2-5k/month and produce the first reproducibility pack.

title: Work-Authorization Continuity Benefit for Care Employers
one_liner: An employer-paid benefit that screens every care worker for legal pathways, tracks EAD renewals and reverification, and plans backfill.
customer: Home-care agencies, nursing homes and assisted-living groups with 50-2,000 workers, especially in NY, FL, MA, MN, WI and CA, and staffing agencies.
problem: 30% of direct care workers are immigrants (60% in New York), and about 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4. At least one in five immigrant direct-care workers come from countries hit by the 75-country visa pause. With turnover already at 77-80%, losing staff means closed beds, and few workers have been screened for family, asylum, adjustment or other pathways.
solution: A per-worker monthly benefit: confidential attorney-led status screening and pathway triage, EAD and renewal tracking with on-time filing, an I-9 reverification calendar with non-discriminatory templates, workforce-at-risk forecasting by site and date, and fast backfill through a partner training school. Employers see aggregate risk, not individual status.
why_now: The 2026 visa pause, TPS terminations and a DOL proposal to roll back home-care wage protections hit at once, and Wisconsin agencies say they're 'just not able to take new clients.' Employers need something other than lobbying.
revenue_model: $8-15 per worker per month (employer-paid), plus filing fees with 20-30% margin and optional filing-fee financing.
non_obvious_insight: Immigration compliance is treated as static HR paperwork, but for care employers it is now a retention and continuity problem. Attorney-led screening can surface pathways that keep workers, which is worth thousands per retained caregiver.
first_30_days: Partner with an immigration law firm and a Haitian community organization, sign three agencies with Haitian-heavy workforces (NY, FL, MA), and pilot with 200 workers.
